newsitem.title: UK: Anglo gold must shed archaic structure - ING.
newsitem.headline: Anglo gold must shed archaic structure - ING.

text.p: Anglo American Corp of South Africa Ltd should merge its gold mines into three or four operations if it is to shed its archaic structure and compete on the world stage, a report from ING Barings said.

The report, listing various scenarios for restructuring, said the merger into three or four operations would create companies large enough to have critical mass while still leaving room for further growth.
"We believe that the opportunity is now open for Anglogold to move forward and some of these changes could be carried out before the end of 1997," the report said.
It suggested a merger into three or four operations by setting up AAC West Wits, AAC Vaal Reefs Complex and Freegold and ERGO.

The report said that the shift to measuring value by market capitalisation per recoverable ounce in gold mining had increased the need for mining companies to raise their resource base every year if they are to demand a high premium and thus increase shareholder wealth.
North American and then Australian gold mines come out on top using this valuation method.
"Each of these companies offer something that a South African gold company generally doesn't -- growth."
It said Barrick Gold had almost twice the market capitalisation of a hypothetical merged Anglogold even though its gold production is only half, and its resource base only 40 percent of Anglogold.

Amalgamating the West Wits mines, Elandsrand and Western Deep Levels, would create a unit producing an annual 1.63 million oz of gold with a market capitalisation of $1.3 billion. It would have a resource base of 49.7 million oz.
A merger between Elandsrand and Deelkraal has already been announced.
The report said Anglo would hold an effective 56.2 percent of the merged operation. Growth at the operation would initially come from the Western Ultra Deep Levels project.

It said the creation of a Vaal Reefs complex would be structurally easier to achieve than the West Wits one. "The market would appreciate a merger of these assets, as the current financial arrangement with royalties and preference shares is very cumbersome."

The enlarged company would be no different to the current set-up as Vaal Reefs currently mines all three lease areas (Eastvaal, Southvaal and Vaal Reefs ). The difference would be that tradeability would be improved, it said.
The envisaged company would include the two areas recently acquired from Gencor ; Weltevreden Gold Mine and Area One East.

The complex would have historical production of 2.2 million oz, rising to 2.8 million oz over three years as Eastvaal increases output. With known mining areas Anglo would effectively control 30.5 percent of the shareholding.
"Another option would be to merge all the Anglogold operations under one listed umbrella. In this way, the whole Anglogold head office would be an integral part of the new company."
It said this company would have a current production rate of 6.1 million oz a year and be the world's largest gold mining company.
"One negative aspect for the company in this scenario is that meaningful growth could only be achieved by adding large new deposits," it said.

It said the whichever route Anglo chose, the merging of gold assets should place a value on management fees, allow Anglo's gold assets to grow as one or more independent companies, increase share tradeability and allow for real growth and a re-rating of the shares.
It said the companies should adopt international financial conventions as soon as possible, including amortisation accounting and retaining income for expansion possibilities.
"In addition, the new companies could pursue exploration programmes not only in South Africa but world-wide, and also enter into mergers and acquisitions."
-- Andrew Gill, London newsroom +171 542 5887
